### Devcon city name for Execution Layer upgrade after Bogotá
[upgrade names are chosen by core devs]

The next execution layer name is undecided. Devcon/Devconnect order suggests it would be [Devconnect 2023](https://devconnect.org/istanbul) in Istanbul, but both [Constantinople](https://ethereum.org/ethereum-forks/#constantinople) and [Istanbul](https://ethereum.org/ethereum-forks/#istanbul) have already been used.

**Skipping to Bangkok is the simplest option.**

https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/devcon-city-name-for-execution-layer-upgrade-after-bogota/30195
On glamsterdam - going to present technical (spec) feedback and status updates from our reachouts. Max 5 mins (excluding any discussion that might come from it)

I’d like to introduce a draft proposal I’m working on for a minimal solution to having native leanSPHINCS signatures on top of frame transactions in Hegota, which is extensible to EIP-8288 (i.e. compatible with leanPCS and later aggregation), which was a concern presented in the last frames breakout call) https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12672

Besu Stance on EIP-8037 and Glamsterdam:

The Besu team recognizes that while EIP-8037 is not a headliner, it is still a critical component of the Glamsterdam release which other EIPs depend on. We do not make this decision in a vacuum with regard to PQ/AI threats, and believe that Hegota should remain focused on that and is orthogonal to Glamsterdam decisions.

We also value the backward-compatible nature of the EVM (not just Ethereum, but all EVM compatible chains) and consider application reliance on our stability a foundational principle.

Our current predicament is a narrow one. We see two options:

1. Delay Glamsterdam and revise the spec for EIP-8037 extremely narrowly to address the new behavior of remaining gas increasing. Sepolia would be sacrificed, but it was end-of-life anyway. 
2. Keep Glamsterdam on schedule, remove EIP-8037 and SFI it into Hegota. This option requires more consideration, so that the other EIPs which interact with EIP-8037 are still assured to be safe. This means a delay for Glamsterdam anyway, and results in minimal benefit from BAL; we'd be nerfing a headliner.

We prefer option 1, and discourage moving forward with breaking changes- we do not rule out possibly needing to do this eventually, however the situation is not that dire and alternative solutions remain.

> Besu Stance on EIP-8037 and Glamsterdam

Thank you @jflo for stating the Besu position. A few questions / clarifications:

> We see two options

You list (1) change EIP-8037, and (2) remove EIP-8037. Of course there is also (3) ship Glamsterdam as-is. You only mention it implicitly as "discourage moving forward with breaking changes" - so does that imply you rank (3) below the other two options?

> Delay Glamsterdam [...] Sepolia would be sacrificed

> Keep Glamsterdam on schedule, remove EIP-8037

For clarification, both of these options would delay Glamsterdam and sacrifice Sepolia, right? The only way to not impact Sepolia and not add further Glamsterdam delays would be (3) to not make changes. So the distinction you make between (1) and (2) seems incorrect on both counts?

> We prefer option 1, and discourage moving forward with breaking changes

Can you clarify this preference? (1) would only allow us to mitigate a minority of affected smart contract breakages, as the majority of them are a consequence of hard coded gas pricing in general, which no modification of EIP-8037 could avoid. That seems incompatible with your simultaneous preference of not moving forward with breaking changes.

Correct, moving forward with breaking changes is the worst option. We expect delays and the sacrifice of Sepolia with both options listed.

The distinction we make between 1 and 2 is of testing volume/complexity. We think just fixing the spec tampers with Glamsterdam the least.

Hard coding gas pricing is an acceptable loss for us, breaking try/catch type functions and problems introduced via increasing gas available are not.
